summary: Iter27 backend sweep: 10/16 passed. WS auth hardening rejects all unauth/non-member traffic (admin bypass works, server logs show membership denied), but 3 tests FAIL because the close-code spec is not met — chat_ws.py calls websocket.close(code=4401) BEFORE accept(), which makes ASGI return HTTP 403 to the client instead of WS close frames with codes 4401/4403. /api/auth/ws-token works correctly (200, expires_in=300, 401 unauth). /api/voice/parse works end-to-end with Gemini (book_taxi single-step + multi-step search_food→open_split_pay verified, 401 unauth). /api/superapp-tips/presets works for taxi + no-service_type + unknown-service. /api/loyalty/levels and /api/loyalty/history FAIL because of an URL collision: routes/loyalty_system.py (registered first, line 306) shadows routes/loyalty.py (line 668) on the same prefix /api/loyalty — server returns the loyalty_system payload (5 levels Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/VIP and history={cashback,coins,level_events}) instead of the new 4-level/{history,count} contract. /api/group/create returns 500 KeyError 'user_id' on the participant-notification loop (existing bug, not introduced by iter27 but blocks the new idempotency contract).

critical.issue: close(code=4401|4403) called BEFORE accept() — ASGI sends HTTP 403 instead of WS close frame. Client cannot read the close code (4401/4403) per spec. Fix: call await websocket.accept() first, then await websocket.close(code=4401, reason=...). Functionally the rejection works (server log: 'chat_ws membership denied / chat_ws auth failed'), but the contract asked for visible 4401/4403 close codes.

Route collision: routes/loyalty_system.py (registered server.py line 306) and routes/loyalty.py (registered line 668) both use prefix='/api/loyalty' with paths /levels and /history. FastAPI keeps the first match → loyalty_system shadows loyalty. Result: /levels returns 5 entries (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/VIP) — not the 4 in the iter27 contract, and /history returns {cashback, coins, level_events} — not {history, count}. Either move the new endpoints to a dedicated prefix (e.g. /api/loyalty-basic) or move loyalty_system_router registration AFTER loyalty_router AND drop the duplicate paths from one of them.

Returns 500 with detail "'user_id'" — KeyError at routes/group_orders.py:41 when iterating participants: `"user_id": participant["user_id"]`. db.users.find_one(..., {"_id":0}) does not project a user_id field on V2 users (their id lives in _id). Use str(participant['_id']) or participant.get('id') (and keep _id projection to extract it). Side effect: the iter27 idempotency check (POST /{group_id}/join twice) is unreachable because creation never succeeds with valid participant emails.

minor.issue: Returned token is created with create_access_token(user_id, email) which uses the global ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE setting (likely > 5 minutes). Response advertises expires_in:300 but the actual JWT exp will be the default. Either pass an explicit ttl=300 or fix the response field to match real expiry.

On JSON decode error the route returns {intents:[], raw, error:'invalid_json'} with status 200. Consider 502 to make client-side fallback more explicit. Also: SYSTEM_PROMPT examples use a typo-tolerant 'Mario\'s' — verified Gemini responds reasonably to both 'Marios' and 'Mario\'s'.

WS /api/chat/ws/{room_id}: admin bypass: any room joinable + history frame received
rejection paths all reject (just with wrong code: HTTP 403 instead of 4401/4403)
POST /api/voice/parse: single-step 'Buche ein Taxi' → intents contains book_taxi
multi-step 'Bestelle Pizza Margherita von Marios und teile mit anna@example.com' → search_food + open_split_pay in correct order, both with action keys among the 11-allowlist
GET /api/superapp-tips/presets: unknown service_type → falls back to default amounts with currency:EUR

action_items: FIX chat_ws.py: call await websocket.accept() before await websocket.close(code=4401|4403) so clients see the documented close codes (Starlette will otherwise downgrade to HTTP 403). Required by the iter27 contract.

FIX /api/loyalty route collision: loyalty_system_router and loyalty_router both bind /api/loyalty/levels and /api/loyalty/history. Either rename loyalty_router prefix (e.g. /api/loyalty-basic) or remove the duplicate paths from loyalty_system.py — currently the iter27 4-level / {history,count} contract is unreachable.

FIX /api/group/create participant lookup at group_orders.py:41 — use str(participant['_id']) (keep _id in projection) or participant.get('id'); without this, /api/group/create returns 500 for any real participant email and breaks the new idempotency test.
CONSIDER passing an explicit ttl=300 in /api/auth/ws-token's create_access_token call so expires_in matches the real JWT exp.
critical_code_review_comments: chat_ws.py L106-122: close-before-accept. ASGI spec: a WS close before accept becomes a synthetic HTTP 403 response. To deliver 4401/4403 to JS clients, accept() first then close(code=...). The membership check itself is solid (taxi_rides/scooter_rentals/food_orders/chats with admin bypass).

loyalty.py and loyalty_system.py both declare `prefix='/api/loyalty'` with overlapping paths — classic registration-order shadowing. P1: pick a single source of truth; right now the new 4-level contract is dead code.

group_orders.py L37-41: db.users.find_one(..., {'_id':0}) drops the only id field on V2 user docs, then participant['user_id'] crashes. Same antipattern likely repeats anywhere participants are looked up by email.
voice.py: f-string in HTTPException(500, f'voice parse error: {e}') leaks the raw LLM/exception detail to clients. Mask in prod or return a generic message + log id.
auth.py /ws-token L293: create_access_token(...) ignores the documented 5-minute lifetime. The 300 in the JSON is currently a lie.

context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes (1) chat_ws accept-before-close, (2) loyalty route collision, (3) group_orders participant['_id'] usage, re-run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter27_sweep.py. The websockets handshake test catches both HTTP-status rejects and WS-close-code rejects via _ws_close_code() which inspects InvalidStatus.response.status_code first then ConnectionClosed.code; once the server calls accept-then-close, the assertion `code == 4401` will pass. The 11-action allowlist in voice.py was verified — Gemini was prompted with 'Bestelle Pizza Margherita von Marios und teile mit anna@example.com' and returned exactly [search_food, open_split_pay] in order, raw text included.
rca of the issue: (1) WS close codes: Starlette's WebSocket.close() before accept() emits a 403 HTTP response to complete the abandoned handshake — the close code parameter is silently ignored because no WS frame channel was ever opened. Fix is two extra lines: accept() then close(code=...). (2) Loyalty collision: server.py imports loyalty_system_router at line 186 / includes at 306, then later imports loyalty_router at 667 / includes at 668. FastAPI's router resolution returns the first match for a given (method, path) pair, so loyalty.py's /levels + /history are unreachable. (3) Group create: V2 users have ObjectId in _id and no separate user_id field; the projection {'_id':0} strips the only id, and the subsequent participant['user_id'] raises KeyError, propagated to FastAPI as 500 with detail "'user_id'". This bug pre-dates iter27 but blocks verifying the iter27 idempotency contract for /api/group/{id}/join.
